top_choice_rationale: The magic-wavelength optical lattice clock (Katori and Ye) is a concrete, quantitative discovery: cancelling the light shift lets thousands of neutral atoms be interrogated free of Doppler and recoil shifts, which opened the 10^-18 regime, reproduced and compared across independent laboratories. The two-name allocation matches distinct roles (concept and first demonstration, record realisation), and a citation naming the magic-wavelength lattice separates it from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes. P002 (magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene) is a strong, well-reproduced discovery but less mature, with unsettled interpretation of the correlated states and credit that leaves out Yuan Cao; it is still preferable to no award.
recusal_note: Director of WACQT and a circuit-QED theorist, so field-proximity to superconducting quantum-computing candidates, but none is on this slate; no connection to Katori, Ye, MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero or Bistritzer apparent from profile.
